# Editorial collage

Newspaper clippings, cut and torn paper, halftone photos, maps and typed labels assembled on a
paper board, the look of Vox explainers and Johnny Harris documentaries. It reads as evidence
being laid out by hand, so it suits investigations, history, money and politics. Palette, paper
stock and density are chosen per brief. Written from references; no film has been made in it with
this skill yet.

## Built in code
- Draw clippings in code (headline type, columns of body text, halftone dot fields) or treat
  sourced images in code. Sourced images are the user's own, public domain or licensed, and are
  listed at delivery.
- Every element has a cut edge: a white or off-white border, a slightly irregular or torn outline,
  a soft drop shadow, so it sits on the board as paper.
- Animate on twos (12 fps) for the stutter, with a slow camera drift and small push-ins.

## Its bar
- **Real artifacts:** headlines, documents, maps and photos of the actual subject, laid out like
  evidence on a desk.
- **Annotation does the pointing:** a marker circle, an underline, an arrow that draws on. One hot
  accent (often red) means "look here" and nothing else.
- **Motion as placement:** pieces slide or drop into place as if a hand set them, overshoot
  slightly and settle; pins drop and wobble once; labels type on.
- **Depth:** stacked paper layers, parallax between them, shadows that grow as a piece lifts.
- **Pace:** pieces arrive on the narration, each answering what was just said.

## Typical failure
A slideshow: one static collage per line with a crossfade. The board is built, marked up and
moved through, piece by piece.
